mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) may lead to tighter monetary conditions, reducing borrowing and spending, which could result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a FEDFUNDS increase, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) may indicate strong demand in the housing market, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 5% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following a HOUST increase, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic output, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by 0.1% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a PAYEMS decrease, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) indicates reduced consumer spending power, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following a RSAFS decrease, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates controlled inflation, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.2% and FEDFUNDS remains stable
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following the specified CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS conditions, the hypothesis is invalidated.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of increasing industrial production (INDPRO) and rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strong economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by 0.3% and PAYEMS increases by 0.1%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following the specified INDPRO and PAYEMS increases, the hypothesis is invalidated.
